mainTopic: Explaining the רבי/רבנן dispute about a doubtful large מנחה vow, then the minimum amounts for pledges of wood, לבונה and metals
overview: The amud opens by asking why רבי and the רבנן disagree about a person who is unsure how big a מנחה he vowed. One problem is raised first: burning an extra handful might break בל תקטירו. It is answered with רבי אליעזר's rule that something may be burned לשום עצים, as fuel. רב אחא's idea that the dispute is about רבי אליעזר's rule is rejected by רב אשי. רבא then explains the dispute through the oil argument between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן. רב אשי explains it as the question of owing a small offering and bringing a big one, and the גמרא shows why that argument must be taught in two places. After a סימן, a new משנה gives the minimum for pledges of wood, לבונה, gold, silver and copper, and lists five cases measured by a קומץ. The גמרא finds sources for wood and לבונה pledges. It then rules that a pledge 'for the מזבח' means לבונה, and begins testing that rule against the עולה and the bird עולה. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the whole offering is obligation, so a second handful is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumed setup. Maybe the entire large מנחה counts as חובה. If so, anything extra burned from it would break the איסור of בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the whole thing is an obligation. And there is a rule: anything that has had part of it put on the fire is covered by 'you shall not burn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is raising a problem with the way the case was just explained. It suggests the whole offering might be one obligation, which would make burning an extra handful forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole מנחה is one חובה, only one קמיצה can be taken from it. Everything else counts as leftover (שיריים). There is a rule that once part of an offering has gone on the fire, burning any other part of it breaks בל תקטירו, so the second handful should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (opens a possible objection)
An obligatory offering, one you must bring
The fires of the מזבח
The prohibition 'you shall not burn' leaven, honey, or leftover parts on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: בל תקטירו here is not only about leaven and honey. The גמרא is using the rule that once part of an offering has gone on the fire, the rest of it is also included in this איסור.

phrases.english: But perhaps all of it is an obligation,
phrases.notes: He means the whole large מנחה might count as one required offering, so only one handful could come from it.

phrases.english: and anything from which part goes to the fires
is included in 'you shall not burn.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of the case given just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that an extra handful may be burned from this large מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole מנחה is one חובה, then after one קמיצה, burning any more of it breaks בל תקטירו.

steps.title: The extra portion is burned as fuel, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the extra portion is not burned as an offering. It is burned only as fuel (לשום עצים). This follows רבי אליעזר, who allows burning forbidden things on the מזבח as wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי said: He burns them as wood, and this follows רבי אליעזר. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, you may not bring them up as a pleasing aroma, but you may bring them up as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the problem from step 1. Burning the extra portion as fuel avoids בל תקטירו, because it is not being offered as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תקטירו forbids burning something as an offering. רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק 'they shall not go up for a pleasing aroma' that the איסור is only on offering it that way. Burning it as plain fuel is allowed, so the problem from step 1 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings up, burns on the מזבח
As wood, burned only as fuel and not as an offering
Pleasing aroma, meaning burned as a real offering

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אליעזר's rule of 'לשום עצים' is the key idea for the rest of this section. The next two steps argue about who in the dispute accepts it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
that he burns them for the sake of wood,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the extra portion that step 1 said would be forbidden to burn.

phrases.english: and this is in line with Rabbi Eliezer.
As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
as a pleasing aroma you may not offer them up,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:12

phrases.english: but you may offer them up for the sake of wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets how the extra portion is burned (as fuel, not as an offering)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the extra handful would break בל תקטירו.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is burned לשום עצים, which רבי אליעזר allows, so there is no איסור.

steps.title: Maybe the real argument is about רבי אליעזר, not about mixing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא son of רבא suggests a new explanation to רב אשי. Maybe everyone agrees you may mix חובה with נדבה. The real disagreement would then be whether we follow רבי אליעזר: the רבנן accept him and רבי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: But maybe everyone agrees it is permitted to mix an obligation with a gift, and here they argue about רבי אליעזר's rule. The רבנן accept רבי אליעזר, and רבי does not accept רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי אליעזר's rule has been brought in, רב אחא asks whether it is the real basis of the dispute between רבי and the רבנן. This would replace the idea that they argue about mixing חובה and נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the dispute was explained as being about mixing חובה with נדבה. רב אחא offers another way to read it: both sides allow mixing, and the only question is whether the extra portion may be burned לשום עצים. If that is right, the whole earlier explanation of the dispute would fall.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
To mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary gift offering
A voluntary gift offering
They disagree
They hold of it / he does not hold of it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps everyone agrees
that it is permitted to mix an obligation with a gift offering,
and here they disagree about Rabbi Eliezer's view:
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי and the רבנן, the two sides of the dispute being explained.

phrases.english: the Rabbis accept Rabbi Eliezer's view,
and Rabbi does not accept Rabbi Eliezer's view?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's rule from step 2 to suggest a different basis for the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי and the רבנן disagree about mixing חובה with נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dispute could just as well be about accepting רבי אליעזר's rule, with both sides allowing mixing.

steps.title: רב אשי shows that רבי cannot allow mixing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the suggestion. If רבי allowed mixing חובה with נדבה, there would be an easy solution. Put sixty in one vessel and one in another, let the vessels touch, and take a קמיצה. So רבי must be against mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you think that according to רבי it is permitted to mix an obligation with a gift, and he does not accept רבי אליעזר, then one could bring sixty in one vessel and one in another vessel, let them touch, and take the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the original explanation of the dispute. He shows that רב אחא's suggestion leads to a result that does not fit רבי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב אחא's reading, רבי would allow mixing and his only worry would be burning an extra handful from one offering. But that worry is easy to avoid. Put the sixty in one vessel and the one in a separate vessel, and take a separate קמיצה from each, with the vessels touching so they count together. Since רבי does not allow this, his reason must be that mixing חובה and נדבה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, meaning if you were to think this
A vessel
He makes them touch
He takes the handful (קמיצה) from the מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: The original explanation stands: רבי and the רבנן disagree about mixing חובה with נדבה. If רבי allowed mixing, the simple setup of sixty in one vessel and one in another, touching, would work.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it enters your mind
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רב אחא.

phrases.english: that according to Rabbi it is permitted to mix an obligation with a gift offering,
and he does not accept Rabbi Eliezer's view,
it would be possible to bring sixty in one vessel,
phrases.notes: Sixty means sixty tenths of flour.

phrases.english: and one in one other vessel,
and make them touch, and take the handful.
phrases.notes: Touching makes the two vessels count as one, so a handful can be taken for each part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לְרַבִּי מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אחא's alternative reading from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the alternative reading leads to a result that does not fit רבי's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבי allows mixing and only rejects רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: If so, the sixty-and-one setup with touching vessels would solve everything. So רבי must hold that mixing חובה with נדבה is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא offers a new explanation of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides allow mixing חובה with נדבה and both accept רבי אליעזר. The real argument is the oil dispute between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees you may mix an obligatory offering with a gift offering, and everyone holds like רבי אליעזר. Here they are really arguing about the dispute between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב אשי rejected the last suggestion, רבא brings a brand-new way to explain why רבי and the רבנן disagree. He is setting up a source he will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that everyone allows mixing חובה with נדבה and that everyone accepts רבי אליעזר. רב אשי's argument in Step 4 assumed that רבי rejects רבי אליעזר, so it does not apply here. רבא moves the disagreement to a different topic: how much oil a large מנחה needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or disagreement

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees it is permitted
to mix an obligatory offering with a gift offering,

phrases.aramaic: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: and everyone holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: This is the רבי אליעזר from Step 2, who allows burning extra parts on the מזבח as wood.

phrases.english: and here, in the dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבָּנַן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and the Rabbis, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי rejects רב אחא בריה דרבא's idea, רבא offers a different explanation that avoids רב אשי's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different underlying מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was thought to be about mixing חובה with נדבה, or about accepting רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides agree on those points. They really disagree about the oil rule of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב versus the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה about oil for a sixty-tenth meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. The רבנן say a sixty-עשרון מנחה gets sixty לוג of oil. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it gets only one לוג, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Even a מנחה of sixty עשרונים gets sixty לוג of oil. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: Even a מנחה of sixty עשרונים gets only its one לוג, as it says, 'for a meal offering, and a log of oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows the oil מחלוקת רבא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן measure oil by flour: one לוג for every עשרון. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב measures oil by offering: each מנחה gets one לוג no matter how big it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the basic flour measure for a מנחה
A liquid measure; here, the oil put into a מנחה
It has only its one לוג of oil

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Even a meal offering of sixty tenths
one puts into it sixty log of oil.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Even a meal offering of sixty tenths
has only its one log,
as it says: 'for a meal offering, and a log of oil.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עִשָּׂרוֹן נוֹתֵן לָהּ שִׁשִּׁים לוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source of the מחלוקת that רבא pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The existence and content of the oil מחלוקת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about sixty עשרונים and the פסוק 'למנחה ולג שמן'

steps.title: The Rabbis follow the sixty-log view
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the רבנן of our משנה hold like the רבנן of the oil משנה. Each עשרון takes its own לוג, so one big sixty-עשרון offering works for any possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold like the רבנן who say sixty לוג: each and every עשרון takes its own לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now applies the oil מחלוקת to the רבנן's side of our dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each עשרון gets its own לוג, the oil comes out right whether the sixty are one offering or two. So bringing one large offering of sixty with sixty לוג causes no problem for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, meaning their opinion is
Each and every one
Takes

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. He means they follow the רבנן of the משנה about the oil.

phrases.english: who say: sixty log,
and each and every tenth
takes its own log.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי כְּרַבָּנַן, דְּאָמְרִי: שִׁשִּׁים לוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted משנה to the רבנן's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking an opinion to an earlier מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear why the רבנן allow one large offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: For them, oil goes by the עשרון, so one large offering of sixty with sixty לוג covers every case.

steps.title: רבי follows the one-log view, which creates the doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that each מנחה gets one לוג. We do not know whether the sixty are one מנחה needing one לוג or two מנחות needing two, so he cannot bring them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who said a מנחה has only its one לוג. We do not know if it is one מנחה, so one לוג is enough, or two מנחות, so we need two לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by showing why רבי's side cannot use one big offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the one-לוג rule, the amount of oil depends on how many offerings there are. In a case of doubt, one large offering might need one לוג or two, and either choice could be wrong. So רבי requires sixty separate offerings, each with its own לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not know
It is enough for it
We need, it is required

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both sides allow mixing חובה with נדבה. The whole dispute comes from the oil rule: oil per עשרון (רבנן) versus one לוג per מנחה (רבי, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי's problem is not mixing חובה with נדבה; רבא says he allows that. His problem is only that he cannot know how much oil to add.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: And Rabbi holds like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
who said it has only its one log,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן אִי חֲדָא מִנְחָה הִיא –
phrases.english: and we do not know whether it is one meal offering,
so one log is enough for it,
or whether they are two meal offerings,
phrases.notes: He means one obligatory offering and one gift offering inside the same sixty.

phrases.english: so we need two logs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, דְּאָמַר אֵין לָהּ אֶלָּא לוּגָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation by giving רבי's side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under רבא's approach, רבי demands sixty separate offerings only because, under the one-לוג-per-מנחה rule, the right amount of oil cannot be known in a case of doubt.

steps.title: רב אשי: they argue about bringing a big offering for a small one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the dispute differently. The רבנן hold that if you owe a small offering and bring a big one, you are יוצא. רבי holds you are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: They argue about someone who owes a small offering and brings a big one. The רבנן hold: if he owes a small one and brings a big one, he has fulfilled his obligation. רבי holds: he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new reason for the argument in our משנה. It is not about oil or mixing. It is about whether a bigger offering covers a smaller vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, one sixty-עשרון מנחה works even if he really vowed less, because the big one covers the small one. רבי says a big offering does not count for a small vow. So the person must bring every possible size separately.

keyTerms.meaning: He owed a small offering and brought a big one instead
He fulfilled his obligation
He did not fulfill his obligation
They argue about

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a third explanation of the same משנה, after the ideas about mixing and oil. It moves the argument to a general rule about offerings.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
They argue about one who owed a small offering and brought a big one.
phrases.notes: Here 'small' and 'big' mean the size of the מנחה, meaning how many עשרונים it has.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
If he owed a small one and brought a big one, he has fulfilled his obligation,
and Rabbi holds: he has not fulfilled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּקָטָן וְהֵבִיא גָּדוֹל קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the רבי/רבנן dispute in place of רבא's oil explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depends on mixing or on how much oil goes with each עשרון
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether a bigger offering counts for a smaller obligation

steps.title: But they already argued about this elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if this is the argument, why repeat it? רבי and the רבנן already argue about 'small and brought big' in another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't they already argue about this once? As we learned: if he owed a small one and brought a big one, he has fulfilled his obligation. רבי says: he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. According to him, the same argument would appear twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a משנה about animals that already teaches this exact argument between רבי and the רבנן. If our משנה is the same argument, it seems to be extra and unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: One time, already once
They argued

phrases.english: But didn't they already argue about it once?
As we learned in a Mishnah:
If he owed a small one and brought a big one, he has fulfilled his obligation,
phrases.notes: This משנה is about animals. He promised a small ox and brought a big one.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: he has not fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's explanation because it makes our משנה repeat another one
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's explanation of the dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same argument is already recorded in the משנה about animals, so teaching it again would be redundant

steps.title: Both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: צריכא: each case teaches something new. From the מנחה alone, we might think the רבנן agree with רבי about animals. From the animal alone, we might think רבי agrees with the רבנן about a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If it were said only about this case (the מנחה), we would say only here the רבנן say he is יוצא, because both small and big give the same קומץ. But there, by animals, where more parts go on the מזבח, say they agree with רבי. And if it were said only about that case (animals), we would say only there רבי says he is not יוצא. But here, say he agrees with the רבנן. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument must be taught in both places. Each case could have been explained in a way that changes the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a מנחה, only a קומץ is burned no matter how big it is, so the רבנן's view is easiest there. With an animal, a bigger animal means more parts burned on the מזבח, so רבי's view is strongest there. Teaching both cases shows that the רבנן hold their view even with animals, and רבי holds his even with a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; both cases teach something
The handful of a מנחה burned on the מזבח
The parts of an animal offering burned on the מזבח
They agree

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the dispute is 'owed small, brought big.' The רבנן say this works, and רבי says it does not. The argument appears for both מנחה and animals because each case could have pushed one side to agree.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'this' and 'that' words. בְּהָא means our מנחה case. הָתָם and בְּהַהִיא mean the animal case.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had been said only about this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is our מנחה case.

phrases.english: it is in this case that the Rabbis say he fulfilled it,
because in both this one and that one it is just a handful;
but there, where the altar portions are larger,
I might say they agree with Rabbi.
And if it had been said only about that case,
it is in that case that Rabbi says he did not fulfill it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָא אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן;
phrases.english: but in this case I might say he agrees with the Rabbis;
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge by showing each case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument in our משנה just repeats the argument in the animal משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has a reason one side might have agreed with the other, so both must be taught

steps.title: A memory list for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן of six words. Each word points to one of the coming משניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory list: wood, gold, wine, burnt offering, thanks offering, bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up what comes next. It gives a short word list to help you remember the order of the upcoming משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No law is taught here. Each word is a hook. עצים matches the next משנה about wood, and זהב matches the gold pledge. The other words point to later משניות about wine, an עולה, a תודה and a שור.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign; a short word list that helps you remember the order of topics

phrases.english: A mnemonic: wood, gold, wine,
burnt offering, thanks offering, bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion and opens the next unit of משניות with a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No law is taught. It is an index of the coming topics.

steps.title: Minimum pledge of wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: Someone who pledges wood must give at least two logs. Someone who pledges לבונה must give at least a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take upon myself to give wood,' he must give at least two logs. If he says 'frankincense,' he must give at least a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the smallest amount you must give when you promise wood or לבונה without naming an amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unspecified pledge still has a minimum: the smallest amount that counts as a real gift of that kind. For wood on the מזבח, that is two logs. For לבונה, it is a קומץ, since that is the measure of לבונה offered elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me'; the wording used to make a vow to bring or give something
Logs or cut pieces of wood for the מזבח fire
Frankincense
A handful; the set measure taken from a מנחה, also used for לבונה

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'It is upon me to give wood' –
he may not give less than two logs;
'frankincense' – not less than a handful.
phrases.notes: The words 'It is upon me' are left out here but assumed: 'It is upon me to give frankincense.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first topic of the memory list, עצים, now appears as a משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified pledge of wood means at least two logs. An unspecified pledge of לבונה means at least a קומץ.

steps.title: The five cases measured by a handful
steps.stepSummary: Since it just mentioned a קומץ of לבונה, the משנה lists all the places where a קומץ is the measure: a לבונה pledge, the לבונה brought with a מנחה, offering a קומץ outside the Temple, and the two bowls of לבונה with the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five handfuls. Someone who pledges frankincense gives at least a handful. Someone who donates a מנחה brings a handful of frankincense with it. Someone who offers a handful outside the Temple is liable. The two bowls of frankincense need two handfuls.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes off on a side topic. Having mentioned a קומץ, it lists every case where a קומץ is the key amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list gathers cases from different areas of the Temple service that share one measure. The first case repeats the rule from the previous step. A person who offers up (מעלה) a קומץ outside the Temple courtyard is liable, and a full קומץ is the amount that makes him liable. The two בזיכין count as two handfuls, which brings the total to five.

keyTerms.meaning: Handfuls; the plural of קומץ
One who donates a meal offering of his own free will
One who offers a sacrifice outside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
The two bowls of לבונה placed with the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: Only four cases are listed, but the משנה says 'five'. The two bowls each need a handful, so they count as two. That makes five.

phrases.english: There are five handfuls:
One who says, 'Frankincense is upon me' –
may not give less than a handful;
one who donates a meal offering –
must bring with it a handful of frankincense;
one who offers up the handful outside is liable;
the two bowls require two handfuls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the word קומץ from the previous step and gathers every case that uses the same measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ is the measure in five cases: a לבונה pledge, the לבונה brought with a מנחה, liability for offering a קומץ outside, and the two בזיכין, which count as two.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'five handfuls' are a list of every case that shares one measure, the קומץ. The two bowls count as two.

steps.title: Minimum pledge of gold, silver and copper
steps.stepSummary: An unspecified pledge of gold means at least a gold דינר. Silver means at least a silver דינר. Copper means copper worth at least a silver מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take upon myself to give gold,' he must give at least a gold דינר. If he says silver, at least a silver דינר. If he says copper, at least the value of a silver מעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה returns to minimum pledges. This time the pledges are metals, which matches the second word of the סימן, זהב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each metal has its own smallest amount that counts as a real gift. For copper, the measure is set by its value, copper worth a silver מעה, not by a copper coin.

keyTerms.meaning: A standard coin; it can be gold or silver
Copper
A small silver coin, worth much less than a דינר

phrases.english: 'It is upon me to give gold' –
he may not give less than a gold dinar;
'silver' – not less than a silver dinar;
'copper' – not less than a silver ma'ah.
phrases.notes: He gives copper, but enough copper to be worth a silver מעה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side list of handfuls, the משנה goes back to minimum pledges, now for metals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified pledge of gold means a gold דינר. Silver means a silver דינר. Copper means copper worth a silver מעה.

steps.title: He named an amount but forgot it
steps.stepSummary: If someone named an amount but forgot what it was, he keeps giving until he can say, 'I surely did not mean this much.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I named an amount, but I do not know what I named,' he must keep giving until he says, 'I did not mean this much.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a person who pledged a specific amount and then forgot the number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual minimum is not enough here, because he may have named more. So he has to cover every amount he might have meant. He stops only when he reaches an amount he is sure is more than his pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I specified'; he named a specific amount when he made the vow
'I intended'; what he meant when he pledged

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when you are unsure how much you owe for a vow, you must give enough to cover every possibility, not just the smallest amount.

phrases.english: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified' –
he must keep bringing until he says,
'I did not intend this much.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from an unspecified pledge to a pledge whose amount was named but then forgotten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who forgot the amount he named must keep giving until he is sure he has passed what he meant.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow with no amount means the minimum. A vow whose named amount was forgotten means giving until he is sure he has covered it.

steps.title: Wood can be pledged as an offering, and the minimum is two logs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word קרבן that a person may pledge wood for the מזבח. If he gives no amount, the minimum is two logs. A פסוק in נחמיה supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: The word 'קרבן' teaches that people may donate wood. How much? Two logs. And so the פסוק says: 'And we cast lots for the wood offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's rule that a person can pledge wood. It also gives the minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word קרבן in the פסוק about a מנחה shows that wood can also be a donation. If no amount was said, the minimum is two logs. The פסוק in נחמיה calling it a 'wood offering' backs up the idea that wood counts as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: People donate voluntarily (a נדבה)
Logs, pieces of wood
The wood offering

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
'An offering' teaches that one may donate wood,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1. The word comes from the פסוק about a מנחה.

phrases.english: And how much? Two logs.
And so it says:
'And we cast lots for the wood offering.'
phrases.notes: נחמיה 10:35

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן קרבן מלמד שמתנדבין עצים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the wood pledge from the משנה in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood may be pledged, and the minimum is two logs.

steps.title: רבי holds that the wood is a real offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the donated wood is a קרבן in every way. It needs salt and it needs הגשה, just like a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: The wood is an offering, so it needs salt and it needs to be brought near the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds that the donated wood is treated like a full קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the word קרבן only to show that wood may be donated. רבי reads it more strongly: the wood is a real קרבן, so the rules of a מנחה apply to it, such as salt and הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt, which is put on every קרבן
Bringing the מנחה to the corner of the מזבח
They require

phrases.english: Rabbi says: Wood is an offering,
it requires salt and requires bringing near.
phrases.notes: Just like a מנחה, which is brought to the corner of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the ברייתא's use of the word קרבן into full קרבן status for the wood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donated wood is a קרבן and needs salt and הגשה.

steps.title: רבא: by רבי's logic, the wood would need קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if רבי treats wood like a מנחה, then it would also need קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And according to רבי, the wood requires קמיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes רבי's view one step further and shows what it leads to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wood is a מנחה for salt and הגשה, then the same comparison should also require taking a handful from it, the way a handful is taken from a מנחה. רבא spells out how far רבי's comparison reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a handful from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
According to the words of

phrases.english: Rava said: And according to the words of Rabbi,
wood requires removal of a handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא ולדברי רבי עצים טעונין קמיצה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from רבי's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the wood needs קמיצה.

steps.title: רב פפא: by רבי's logic, the wood needs other wood to burn on
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that according to רבי, the wood offering must be burned on top of other wood, like any קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: According to רבי, the wood needs wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another consequence of רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every קרבן is burned on the wood of the מזבח's fire. If the donated wood is itself a קרבן, it cannot count as its own fire wood, so it must be placed on other wood.

keyTerms.meaning: They need

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: According to the words of Rabbi,
wood needs wood.
phrases.notes: He means the donated wood must be put on top of other wood to burn, like any קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב פפא לדברי רבי עצים צריכין עצים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second consequence after רבא's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the wood offering must be burned on other wood.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי treats donated wood as a real קרבן. רבא and רב פפא show what follows: it would need קמיצה and would need other wood to burn on.

steps.title: What is the source that לבונה must be at least a קומץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a לבונה pledge is at least a קומץ, and asks how we know this.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'לבונה: not less than a קומץ.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a minimum amount for a לבונה pledge without a reason. The גמרא wants a פסוק that sets the קומץ as the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not give less
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Frankincense: he may not give less than a handful.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 13.

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from wood to the next rule in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the קומץ minimum for לבונה

steps.title: A הקש links לבונה to the handful taken from a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places 'his handful' next to 'all the לבונה,' so לבונה is compared to the קמיצה of a מנחה. Just as that is a קומץ, a לבונה pledge is at least a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall take up from it with his handful, from the flour of the מנחה and from its oil, and all the לבונה.' The פסוק compares לבונה to the taking up from a מנחה. Just as that is a קומץ, so too לבונה is a קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and a הקש, a comparison the Torah makes by placing two things side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 6:8, the handful taken from the מנחה and the לבונה appear in one sentence. Because the Torah links them, the measure of one, a קומץ, becomes the measure of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, using a הקש (a link the Torah makes by putting two things side by side)
Taking up, here the handful removed from the מנחה
Fine flour
So too, also

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And he shall take up from it with his handful,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:8

phrases.english: 'from the fine flour of the meal offering and from its oil,'
'and all the frankincense.'
It compares frankincense to the taking up from a meal offering:
just as the taking up from a meal offering is a handful,
so too frankincense is also a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש from ויקרא 6:8 links לבונה to the קומץ of a מנחה

steps.title: A pledge 'to the מזבח' with nothing named means לבונה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who pledged 'to the מזבח' without naming anything brings לבונה. Only לבונה goes entirely onto the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If one says, 'It is upon me for the מזבח,' he brings לבונה, because nothing goes onto the מזבח except לבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא deals with a vague pledge 'for the מזבח' and decides what it obligates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other offerings are partly eaten or partly given to the כהנים. לבונה alone is burned entirely on the מזבח. So a pledge made simply 'for the מזבח' is understood as a pledge of לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Onto the מזבח itself

phrases.english: The Sages taught: 'It is upon me for the altar':
he must bring frankincense,
because you have nothing that is offered
entirely on the altar except frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of לבונה pledges with a new ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unnamed pledge 'for the מזבח' means לבונה.

steps.title: He named something but forgot what: he brings everything
steps.stepSummary: If he named a specific item for the מזבח but forgot what it was, he must bring one of every kind of thing that is offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified': he brings from everything that is offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second case: the person did name an item but cannot remember which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we cannot assume he meant לבונה, because he says he named something particular. To be sure he has kept his נדר, he must bring every type that could have been meant. This is similar to step 16, where a forgotten amount is covered by giving more.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified, I named it clearly
From every kind of item

phrases.english: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified':
he must bring from everything that is offered on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts an unnamed pledge with a named but forgotten pledge
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forgotten specific pledge requires bringing every type offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatToRemember: A pledge with nothing named means לבונה. If he named something and forgot it, he brings every possible type.

steps.title: Isn't an עולה also entirely burned on the מזבח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that only לבונה goes entirely onto the מזבח, pointing to the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really nothing else that goes entirely on the מזבח? But there is the עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason the ברייתא gave in step 23. An עולה seems to be completely burned on the מזבח too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said an unclear pledge 'to the מזבח' means לבונה, because nothing else goes entirely onto the מזבח. If an עולה also goes entirely onto the מזבח, that reason falls apart. The person could have meant an עולה just as easily.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing else?
But isn't there...? (a challenge pointing to a counterexample)
Burnt offering, which is burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And is there nothing else?
phrases.notes: He means nothing else besides לבונה that goes entirely onto the מזבח, as the ברייתא claimed.

phrases.english: But there is the burnt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only לבונה goes entirely onto the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה is also burned completely, so לבונה is not the only such item.

steps.title: The עולה's hide goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: An עולה is not entirely given to the מזבח, because its hide is given to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is its hide, which goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an עולה does not count, because part of it, the hide, is not burned. It goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Entirely onto the מזבח' means nothing at all is left over for anyone else. The meat of an עולה is burned, but its hide is given to the כהנים. So לבונה is still the only thing that is given completely to the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hide, the skin of the animal
The priests who serve in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: There is its hide, which goes to the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the עולה is not totally given to the מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An עולה is completely burned, just like לבונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hide of an עולה goes to the כהנים, so it is not entirely for the מזבח.

steps.title: Isn't a bird burnt offering entirely burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about an עולת העוף, which seems to be burned completely, skin included.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the bird burnt offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new counterexample, the bird burnt offering. Its skin is not given to the כהנים, so the answer from step 26 does not work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about the hide only worked for an animal עולה. A bird עולה is burned with its skin, so it seems nothing is left for the כהנים. That would again make לבונה not the only item that goes entirely onto the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird burnt offering

phrases.english: But there is the bird burnt offering,
phrases.notes: Unlike an animal עולה, a bird's skin is not given to the כהנים, so the last answer doesn't help here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that gets around the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only לבונה goes entirely onto the מזבח, even after the answer about the hide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bird עולה has no hide given to the כהנים, so it seems to go entirely onto the מזבח.

steps.title: The answer begins: 'There are...'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts answering the question about the bird עולה. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with the word 'there are'. It is about to name parts of the bird that are not burned on the מזבח, and the rest comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer uses the same pattern as step 26. It points to some part of the offering that does not go onto the מזבח, so the bird עולה is not 'entirely' for the מזבח either.

keyTerms.meaning: There is / there are

phrases.english: There are
phrases.notes: The answer is cut off here. The next amud finishes the sentence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction, using the same pattern as step 26 (finished in the next section).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird עולה goes entirely onto the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some parts of the bird do not go onto the מזבח (named in the next section).
